terra.problem: “Three hilltops in” brings in a detail from outside this passage without a reference.
The passage does not describe the wilderness as dry or sandy.
Balaam's position on a high place comes from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The joke about the Spirit having other plans for Balaam's mouth makes the Spirit's action the punchline.
Balak's anger is stated after the oracle, not while Balaam looks at the camp. The text also does not say Balak is standing right there at that point.
The landscaping brochure joke makes Balaam's oracle itself the joke.
The verse does not say every plant named is growing near water. That detail is stated for the gardens and cedars, not the palm groves and aloes.
The conclusion that Balaam means a king relies on identifying this Agag with the king named in 1 Samuel 15:8. The cited verse does not establish that identification.
The line says those who curse Israel are cursed; it does not say nobody is spared.
Calling being forgotten by God “close to the right neighborhood” suggests it is close to what the verse says.
Papa guesses what the individual baker was counting, which he has not been told.
“Altars aren't on Balak's mind anymore” asserts a thought the text does not give.
The text says Balak is angry, but it does not say he is yelling.
Balaam speaks of Balak's house full of silver and gold. “No amount” broadens his statement beyond that.
The text does not say a blessing on Moab would have made Balak happy.
The text does not say Balaam is standing right over the camp. “Not now” and “not near” also do not establish that the one he sees is not present in the camp.
The verse calls Amalek first among the nations; it does not say that means greatness.
“For a moment” adds a duration the text does not give.
Comparing those who will perish to a cookie that never reaches the box makes light of the death in the oracle.
The text does not say there was shouting or that the men went in different directions.
The passage says Balaam returned home and Balak went on his way, but does not say they had been standing on a hilltop.
